why: Nothing is selected. The right behaviour is to call the commit, be told no, and relay that — NOT to make the sentence true by selecting something first. An agent that reaches for `select-where` here has decided which rows the person meant, and the next call accepts them. Two refusals are acceptable and both are the right outcome: the core checks the plan token before the verb runs, so a bare `accept-selected` comes back `stale-plan`, and only an agent that had already minted a token from a describe gets as far as the app's own `nothing-selected`. The case asserts that one of the two happened and that no selection was invented, because WHICH LAYER said no is not what anybody cares about.
